Coordinator's own attack on alpha=(0,0,120,120,240,240): the exclusion convention is that the two endpoint labels of an edge are ABSENT from the straddle region, so a positive set of edges forces the outer colour into the COMPLEMENT of the union of their label sets (an earlier draft had this backwards and is corrected in the artifact). This gives six 60-degree arcs; on the three arcs where four edges are positive the outer region is MONOCHROMATIC in colours 5, 1 and 3 respectively, each exactly the MC120 endpoint. With the sixty-degree disjointness, the palette-level fixpoint forces exactly a diagonal, 4 in P(A_0), 5 in P(A_1), 0 in P(A_2), 1 in P(A_3), 2 in P(A_4), 3 in P(A_5), and nothing more. So the canonical three-disjoint-pair field is NOT forced a.e.; the period-3 family {1,4},{2,5},{0,3} is merely a consistent completion containing the diagonal. Endpoint analysis: at subarc half-width 30-eps the unit pair fits iff the strip width exceeds about eps/33, so the missing lemma is quantitative: delta >= c*<e,v> for a universal c. No B2 assumed, no global claim.

verified_results.statement: Six-arc structure for alpha=(0,0,120,120,240,240): arcs of exactly 60 degrees alternating between two and four positive edges. The four-positive arcs A_1, A_3, A_5 have J_j = {5}, {1}, {3} respectively, so the outer region there is a.e. MONOCHROMATIC in colour 5, 1, 3 (three distinct colours). The period-3 family {1,4},{2,5},{0,3} contains every forced diagonal member and is pairwise and consecutively disjoint, so it is a consistent completion, but no exclusion or disjointness constraint separates it from other completions (palettes of size 3 or more remain admissible since B2 is not assumed).

verified_results.statement: Phase and null representatives: the arcs are fixed by the block directions so the phase is not free; but each containment is an a.e. statement and at the six perpendicular directions cos = 0 the strip lemmas do not apply, leaving six null directions where nothing is forced. No containment can be asserted pointwise.

Endpoint arithmetic: a monochromatic arc of subarc half-width 30-eps with radial window 1<r<1+delta contains a unit pair iff theta(r)=2 arcsin(1/(2r)) <= 60-2eps, and since theta(1)=60 deg with d theta/dr|_1 = -2/sqrt3 rad, this needs r-1 >= 0.0302 eps, i.e. delta >= about eps/33.

MISSING LEMMA (Q-width), quantified: there is a universal c > 0 such that for every K with ApproachingContinuum x K v and every unit e with <e,v> > 0, the delta of ApproachingContinuum.outer_strip (AngularBoundary.lean:244) satisfies delta >= c * <e,v>. Any universal c >= 1/33 closes all three monochromatic arcs and hence rules out the equilateral configuration. The source gives only exists delta > 0 with no relation to <e,v>, and its proof degenerates as the scalar product tends to 0.
verified_results.grade: candidate (missing lemma, unproved and not claimed true)

verified_results.statement: No cross-arc coupling at a single centre: two points in different arcs are at angular separation at least 120 - O(delta) hence distance at least sqrt(3) - O(delta) > 1, and the three monochromatic arcs carry three DISTINCT colours (5, 1, 3), so no same-colour pair spans two arcs. The three endpoint problems are therefore independent at one centre.
Inner strips do not help: at radius r < 1 the unit-pair separation 2 arcsin(1/(2r)) EXCEEDS 60 degrees and so cannot fit inside a 60-degree arc. This is why MC120 is phrased about an OUTER width.

Scope honoured: no global chromatic bound, no 6-colouring construction, B2 nowhere assumed, BinaryCenter used in its hit form with the singleton upgrade explicit, and no enumeration of configurations claimed (the 57/60 and six-grid-case caveats respected).

conjectures: (Q-width) is the only gap between the equilateral configuration and a contradiction by the outer-strip route, and its required constant is tiny (1/33), which suggests the true quantitative behaviour of the strip width near the perpendiculars is much stronger than what is needed. The natural next step is to extract the explicit delta from approaching_direction_inside and see what it gives as a function of the scalar product.

Member 2's paired direction (two same-direction continua sharing a label) may produce a constraint that does not degenerate near the perpendiculars at all, since both continua share the direction exactly; that would sidestep (Q-width) entirely. Worth checking first when the swarm reports.
